title.en: Read uptime from your own device

why.en: Sends one GetRequest for sysUpTime to your own router or a Linux box with snmpd. Use only devices you own and have a community for.
why.hinglish: Aapke apne router ya snmpd wale Linux box ko sysUpTime ke liye ek GetRequest bhejta hai. Sirf wahi devices use karo jo aapke hain aur jinka community aapko pata hai.

expect.en: Needs the Net-SNMP tools and an agent on that address. You get a line like DISMAN-EVENT-MIB::sysUpTimeInstance = Timeticks: (123456789) 14 days, 6:56:07.89. With no agent or a wrong community it prints 'Timeout: No Response', exactly like the wrong-community scenario. Output varies.
expect.hinglish: Net-SNMP tools aur us address par agent chahiye. DISMAN-EVENT-MIB::sysUpTimeInstance = Timeticks: (123456789) 14 days, 6:56:07.89 jaisi line milti hai. Agent na ho ya community galat ho to 'Timeout: No Response' print hota hai, bilkul wrong-community scenario jaisa. Output alag ho sakta hai.

why.en: Open the downloaded .pcap and read the community string and OIDs.
why.hinglish: Download kiya .pcap kholo aur community string aur OIDs padho.

expect.en: You see get-request, get-response and the linkDown trap. In v2c packets the community string is readable in the details; in the SNMPv3 capture the PDU shows as encrypted.
expect.hinglish: get-request, get-response aur linkDown trap dikhte hain. v2c packets mein community string details mein padhne laayak hai; SNMPv3 capture mein PDU encrypted dikhta hai.

why.en: Traps go to UDP 162 instead of 161.
why.hinglish: Traps 161 ke bajaye UDP 162 par jaate hain.

expect.en: Only the unasked SNMPv2-Trap packet for linkDown remains.
expect.hinglish: Sirf linkDown ka bina maanga SNMPv2-Trap packet bachta hai.
